standard.title: Select structures for purpose
standard.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, selecting subject matter, and using text structures, language features, literary devices and visual features as appropriate to convey information, ideas and opinions in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts using paragraphs, complex sentences, expanded verb groups, tense, topic-specific vocabulary, punctuation and visual features (AC9E6LY06). They have not yet worked at the level of deliberately selecting text structures, language features and literary devices to convey specific purposes — the move from using these elements to selecting them purposefully.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create and publish texts selecting structures, language features and literary devices for purpose.

nodes.label: Planning with purpose in mind
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a text by identifying its purpose, audience and the structural and language choices that will serve them
nodes.minimum_width: Given a writing task, identify the purpose and audience; name at least one text structure and one language feature that would be appropriate and explain why
nodes.typical_width: Plan a text by mapping purpose and audience to structural choices and language features — what text type, what stages, what vocabulary register, what sentence complexity is appropriate, and why each choice serves the purpose
wider: Compare how the same subject matter would be planned differently for different purposes — an imaginative recount vs a persuasive argument vs an analytical response — and discuss how purpose drives every planning decision
Examine how compiling a portfolio of texts for a common concept or audience requires consistent structural and language choices across different text types
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot connect purpose and audience to structural and language choices at the planning stage, Nodes 2 and 3 lack the deliberate decision-making frame — creation and editing both depend on having an articulated intention to evaluate against.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly plan what to write (content) without planning how to write it (structure and language). The reasoning scaffold — purpose → audience → appropriate structure → appropriate language features — establishes the decision chain that makes planning purposeful rather than content-listing.

success_criteria: Identifies the purpose and audience for a given writing task
Names at least one structural and one language feature choice that serves the purpose and explains why

nodes.label: Creating for purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a written or multimodal text, making deliberate choices about text structures, language features and literary devices to serve the purpose and audience
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text for a given purpose and identify at least two deliberate structural or language choices made during drafting; explain what each choice contributes to the purpose
nodes.typical_width: Create a written or multimodal text demonstrating deliberate selection of text structures, language features and literary devices — explaining how each choice serves the purpose and is appropriate for the audience
wider: Compare how the same subject matter is created differently for different purposes — an imaginative recount vs a persuasive argument vs an analytical response — examining how purpose drives every structural and language decision
Create a multimodal text that combines print, visual and audio elements, explaining how each mode contributes to the purpose

response_modes.reason: Creating a text brings together planning, knowledge of text structures, language feature selection, and literary device use into a coordinated drafting process. The integration is the point — not any single component skill but their coordinated application in service of a communicative purpose.

success_criteria: Creates a text that demonstrates at least two deliberate structural or language choices
Explains what each choice contributes to the purpose of the text

nodes.label: Editing and publishing for purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit a draft text by making purposeful revision decisions, and publish in a form appropriate to the audience and purpose
nodes.minimum_width: Given a draft text, identify at least one revision decision — something changed, added or removed — and explain why the change better serves the purpose; identify an appropriate form or platform for publishing
nodes.typical_width: Edit a written or multimodal text by making deliberate revision decisions — removing unnecessary repetition, reordering for logic or effect, varying sentence structure, refining language choices — and explain how each decision improves the text; select a publication form appropriate to the audience and purpose
wider: Edit for meaning using digital tools (tracked changes, collaborative editing) to make the revision decision-making process visible and discussable
Compile a portfolio of texts for a shared concept or audience, editing across the collection for consistency of structural and language choices

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat editing as error-correction rather than purposeful revision. The reasoning scaffold — what was changed, why was it changed, how does the change better serve the purpose — shifts editing from a mechanical check to a meaning-making process and builds the metalinguistic awareness that transfers across all writing contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Purposeful editing is where metalinguistic awareness is most visible — advancing students who articulate revision decisions develop a transferable reflective practice. The tracked-changes and portfolio directions make the decision process explicit and discussable, extending the value beyond a single text.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one revision decision in editing a draft and explains how it better serves the purpose
Selects a publication form appropriate to the audience and purpose
